PMF.finiteProduct: Given finitely many laws pᵢ on finite coordinate alphabets, their product is the joint law of independent draws from the respective pᵢ. A vector x has mass ∏ᵢ pᵢ(xᵢ).
PMF.finiteProduct_apply: The probability of the vector x under the finite product law is the product ∏ᵢ pᵢ(xᵢ) of its coordinate probabilities.
PMF.mem_support_finiteProduct_iff: A vector x has positive mass under the finite product law if and only if each coordinate xᵢ has positive mass under pᵢ.
PMF.finiteProduct_map_eval: The i-th coordinate marginal of the product of the laws pⱼ is pᵢ.
PMF.finiteProduct_of_isEmpty: Over an empty index set, the finite product law is the point mass on the unique empty vector.
PMF.finiteProduct_pure: Taking the product of point masses at the coordinates aᵢ gives the point mass at the vector a.
PMF.finiteProduct_map_reindex: Relabel the indices of a vector of independent coordinates by a bijection e from J to I. The relabeled coordinates are independent, and the law at j is the original law at e(j).
PMF.finiteProduct_map_restrict: Select coordinates of a vector of independent draws using an injection e from J into I. The selected coordinates are independent, and the law of the j-th selection is the original law at e(j).
PMF.finiteProduct_map_sum: Split the finite index set into disjoint blocks I and J. Under the product law, the two subvectors are independent and each has the product of its own coordinate laws.
PMF.finiteProduct_map_pair: For distinct indices i and j, the joint law of the i-th and j-th coordinates of a product law is the independent product of pᵢ and pⱼ.
